info.title: Lumos API (v1)
info.description:
Lumos API v1 is the programmatic interface to your connected apps, the entitlements on them, and
the workflows that grant access to those entitlements.

Every path is prefixed with `/v1`. Authenticate with an API token, which inherits the permissions
of the user who created it: a call returns what that user could see in the Lumos UI, and nothing
more.

New here? Browse what you can connect with `GET /v1/integrations`, read the credentials an
integration expects with `GET /v1/integrations/{app_class_id}/connection-schema`, then connect it
with `POST /v1/apps`.

Every list endpoint shares one pagination contract. Set the page length with `page_size`, then send
the `next_page_token` from a response back as `page_token` to fetch the next page. A `null`
`next_page_token` means you have reached the end.

Every error shares one envelope. Branch on the machine-readable `code`, not on `detail`.

v1 is in beta: it is enabled per organization, and paths and payloads can still change.

post.description:
Create an access policy. Returns 201 with the created policy. Grant entitlements by Entitlement UUID under `apps[].entitlements`, or leave them out to grant access to the app itself. Send `is_everyone_condition: true` for a policy that applies to everyone, or an `access_condition` for one that doesn't; sending both returns 400. The everyone condition a read returns in `access_condition` counts as `is_everyone_condition: true`, so a body built from a read can be sent back as is.

An `access_condition` may use only the attributes and operators the Lumos condition builder offers, with one operator per attribute, and a date-time value needs a time zone offset (`2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Any other condition returns 400 naming each problem.

A policy is created as a draft unless `status` is `published`. A draft can't be enabled, so sending `is_enabled: true` without `status: published` returns 400. Creating a published policy whose condition matches another published policy also returns 400. A draft with the same condition is allowed. When your organization requires approval before publishing, `status: published` returns 400.

Listing an app twice, or an entitlement twice under one app, returns 400. An app or entitlement that doesn't resolve returns 404 without saying which.

post.description:
Run the sync for one app review, optionally replacing its scope filters in the same call.

The sync runs asynchronously: the request returns `202 Accepted` with an operation. Poll `GET /v1/operations/{id}` until `done` is true.

Rebuilding the subject set is what re-scoping means. Reviewer assignments survive for subjects that survive; subjects that fall out of scope take their assignments with them. A caller that re-scopes after assigning should re-check how many subjects are still unassigned before launching.

Only an app review at or before `assigning-reviewers` can be synced — once the review has launched, reviewers hold decisions a sync would invalidate.

get.description:
List the fields this app review's subjects can be filtered on, each with its datatype, the operators that datatype permits, and — for a field drawn from a fixed set — the values it accepts.

Read this before building a `filters` array: the filterable set depends on what the app's data carries and on how far the review has progressed, so it is only known at runtime. A decision filter appears once the review has launched, and a removal filter once removals have started.

Copy an option's `value` verbatim into `values`; `label` is display-only and is rejected as a value. Values are always strings, so a numeric or date argument is `["90"]` rather than `[90]`.

This list isn't paginated.

Fields whose values are open-ended — permission, reviewer, manager, team, title, entitlement type — are not listed here yet.

get.description:
Read one subject: what is being reviewed, who is reviewing it, what they decided, and what removal that decision led to.

What a subject is follows from the app review's type — an accounts review reviews accounts, an entitlements review reviews the entitlements an account holds — and `subject_type` says which. An entitlement subject also names the account it belongs to, so one shape serves both.

`removal.status` is current even while the removal runs. Evidence is reported beside `removal` rather than in it (`is_evidence_attached`, `evidence_required_by`, and the files under `expand=evidence`), since an approved subject can owe evidence too.

`removal.error` says which capability failed and what the integration reported. It does not say whether retrying will help; a removal waiting on a person clears only once that person acts.

post.description:
Create a custom app, or connect an integration.

Omit `app_class_id`, or send `custom`, to create a custom app — one Lumos has no connector for, whose accounts you maintain yourself. It needs `label_override`, `category_override` and `description_override`. Any other `app_class_id` instead connects that integration using the credentials in `auth`; which keys are required varies by integration, so read them from `GET /v1/integrations/{app_class_id}/connection-schema` rather than hardcoding them. `auth`, `settings` and `version` only apply with `app_class_id`.

condition.description:
Who this rule pre-approves, and for how long they can have access.

A condition is either a single check or several checks combined. A single check looks like `{"attribute": {"label": "<name>", "value": "<path>"}, "<operator>": <value>}` and uses exactly one operator. To require every check to match, wrap them in `{"and": [...]}`. To require at least one to match, wrap them in `{"or": [...]}`. To match the opposite of a check, wrap it in `{"not": {...}}`.

Only the attributes below are accepted, and each one accepts only the operators listed for it. Any other attribute or operator returns 400.

- `identity.groups[*].external_id` accepts `contains_any`. The value is a list of `{"label": "<group name>", "value": "<group ID>"}`, where the group ID is the ID the group has in the app it comes from. The check matches a person who belongs to any of the listed groups.
- `identity.email`, `identity.team`, `identity.title`, and `identity.status` accept `equals`, `!=`, `in`, `exists`, `contains`, `starts_with`, and `ends_with`.
- `identity.start_date` and `identity.end_date` accept `equals`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `in`, and `exists`.
- `identity.source_app.id` accepts `equals`, `!=`, `in`, and `exists`.
- `identity.custom_attributes["<Key>"]` checks a custom attribute your organization has defined. For an attribute whose value is a person, use `identity.custom_attributes["<Key>"].id`. For an attribute whose value is a group, use `identity.custom_attributes["<Key>"].external_id`. It accepts the same operators as the attributes above that have the same value type. To match any of several values, use `in` with a list of `{"label": "<display name>", "value": "<value>"}`.
- `webhook.responses["<webhook ID>"]` checks the response of one of your organization's pre-approval webhooks, which is called when the request is evaluated. It accepts only `equals` with the value `"PREAPPROVED"`, and can't be inside a `not`. The check matches when the webhook pre-approves the request.
- `identity.oncall["<schedule ID>"].on_call` checks whether the person is on call for an on-call schedule when the request is evaluated. The schedule ID is the schedule's entitlement ID. It accepts only `equals` with the value `true`, and can't be inside a `not`.
- `access_request.access_length` accepts `equals`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, and `in`. Values are in seconds, for example `{"label": "<display name>", "value": <seconds>}`. To match unlimited access, use the value `2147483647` (2**31 - 1). Leaving this attribute out allows any duration, unlimited included.

`null` when the rule is limited by a webhook, an on-call schedule, or an access policy instead. This API can't show those limits.

tags.name: Access Policies
tags.description:
An access policy grants apps, and optionally specific entitlements on them, to the identities that
qualify under its `access_condition`, a Lumos Condition object.

`POST /v1/access-policies` creates a policy and returns 201. `GET /v1/access-policies` lists
policies, and `GET`, `PUT`, and `DELETE` on `/v1/access-policies/{access_policy_id}` read, replace,
and delete one.

Each entitlement a policy grants appears under `apps[].entitlements[]`, identified by its
Entitlement UUID, the `id` that `GET /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}` returns.

tags.name: Access Requests
tags.description:
An access request asks for access to an app, or to specific entitlements on it, for you or for
another user.

- `POST /v1/access-requests` creates requests, naming entitlements by Entitlement UUID in
  `entitlement_ids`, and returns them as a list.
- `GET /v1/access-requests` and `GET /v1/access-requests/{id}` read requests.
- `POST /v1/access-requests/{id}:cancel` cancels a pending request.

Of the built-in roles, Admin, Read Only Admin, AppStore Read Only Admin, and App Admin can read
every access request in your organization. Anyone else sees only the requests they made and the
ones made for them.

tags.name: Access Reviews
tags.description:
An access review is a campaign that reviews who has access to what across your connected apps.
Each app in a campaign is an app review.

v1 has two access-review endpoints so far, both scoped to one app review:

- `GET /v1/access-reviews/{review_uuid}/apps/{app_review_uuid}/subject-filters` lists the fields
  you can filter the app review's subjects on. Each field comes with the operators it supports
  and, when it has a fixed set of values, the values it accepts.
- `POST /v1/access-reviews/{review_uuid}/apps/{app_review_uuid}:sync` runs the app review's data
  import, optionally with new scope filters. It returns 202 with an operation. Poll
  `GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}` until `done` is true.

You can't create, list, or update campaigns in v1 yet. Lumos enables these endpoints per
organization, separately from the rest of v1, so contact your Lumos representative to turn them on.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description:
An account is a person's presence inside a connected app. Accounts arrive through sync; you cannot
create one through this API.

`GET /v1/accounts/{account_uuid}/entitlements` lists what one account holds. It reads the same
relationship as `GET /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}/accounts`, from the account's side rather
than the entitlement's.

tags.name: Activity Logs
tags.description:
Activity logs record the actions taken across your organization's apps and identities.
`GET /v1/activity-logs` lists them, newest first.

Reading activity logs requires permission to view them across your organization. Of the built-in
roles, Admin and Read Only Admin have it. Without it, the request returns 403.

tags.name: App Categories
tags.description:
App categories are the fixed set of categories an app can belong to, such as `Developers`.
`GET /v1/app-categories` lists them as `{label}` objects.

A `label` is the exact value to send as `category` to `POST /v1/apps` and
`PATCH /v1/apps/{app_uuid}`. It is also the value the app read endpoints report. Read the list
instead of hard-coding it.

tags.name: Apps
tags.description:
An app is an integration you have connected, one per connected instance of a service. Your Okta
tenant is an app. A second Slack workspace is a second app.

### Connecting one

1. `GET /v1/integrations/{app_class_id}/connection-schema` to see which `auth` and `settings`
   keys the integration expects.
2. `POST /v1/apps` with those credentials. Apps whose credentials validate right away connect, and
   their first sync waits for an admin to review match rules. It starts from the Lumos UI, or from
   `POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:sync` with `skip_first_sync_review: true`. Apps that need browser
   consent are finished in the Lumos UI.
3. `GET /v1/apps/{app_uuid}` to follow the first sync. `sync_status` shows the state of the
   app's most recent sync. A sync started with `POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:sync` also returns an
   operation, which you poll with `GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}`.
4. `POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:sync` to resync later. Only one sync runs per app at a time, so a
   second request while one is in flight returns 409.

Rotate credentials with `PATCH /v1/apps/{app_uuid}`, which also updates an app's metadata.
`POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:disconnect` drops the stored credentials and returns the app to a
connectable state; `DELETE /v1/apps/{app_uuid}` removes the app outright.

### Reading apps

`expand` is opt-in and evaluated per field: ask for `admins`, `custom_attributes`,
`appstore_settings`, or any of the three workflow fields. A field you lack permission to read is
left out of the response instead of failing the whole request, so a 200 does not prove every field
you asked for came back.

To list only the connected apps you manage through the API, combine `connection_source=api` with
`disconnected=false`.

### Bound workflows

Each app carries three bindings: an approval workflow, a default provisioning workflow, and a
default deprovisioning workflow. The two `default_` workflows are the ones that entitlements on
the app fall back to. To bind a workflow to one entitlement instead, use the Entitlements
endpoints.

tags.name: Custom Attribute Definitions
tags.description:
Custom attributes are the extra fields your organization keeps on users. These endpoints read
their *definitions*, not the values stored against any particular user.

`GET /v1/custom-attribute-definitions` returns one entry per label, unified across every app that
supplies it. Narrow the list with `source_type` to tell attributes synced from an app apart from
ones your team created, or with `app_id` to see only what a single app supplies.

tags.name: Entitlements
tags.description:
An entitlement is a grantable unit of access on an app: a role, a license tier, a group, a
permission. Accounts hold entitlements.

- `POST /v1/entitlements` creates a requestable entitlement on an app.
- `GET /v1/apps/{app_uuid}/entitlements` lists the entitlements on one app.
- `GET /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}/accounts` lists who currently holds one.
- `PATCH /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}` updates its `label`, `description`, and
  `custom_approval_message_override`. Sending any other field returns 400.
- `DELETE /v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}` refuses while the entitlement is still held,
  returning 409 with an `active_accounts` count.

### Per-entitlement workflows

An entitlement can have its own approval override, provisioning workflow, and deprovisioning
workflow, bound to it rather than to the whole app. Each has a GET and a PUT, and the approval
override also has a DELETE that turns it off.

An entitlement that can't be requested returns 404 with
`Workflows are not available for this entitlement.` on each of these endpoints.

tags.name: Groups
tags.description:
Lumos syncs groups from your connected apps, such as your Okta groups, and these endpoints read
them.

- `GET /v1/groups` lists groups. Filter by `name` (add `exact_match=true` to require an exact
  match), by `integration_specific_id` (the group's ID in the source system), or by `app_id`.
- `GET /v1/groups/{group_id}` reads one group, and `GET /v1/groups/{group_id}/users` lists its
  members.

An `app_id` that matches no app in your organization returns 404.

tags.name: Identity Events
tags.description:
Identity events are the changes Lumos detects on your organization's identities, such as a change
to a status, a group membership, or a custom attribute. `GET /v1/identity-events` lists them.
Narrow the list with `identity_ids`, `changed_fields`, `start_time`, and `end_time`.

A page can come back empty while `next_page_token` is still set, because events Lumos can't read
are dropped after a page is fetched. Keep paging until `next_page_token` is absent, not until a
page is empty.

tags.name: Inline Webhooks
tags.description:
Inline webhooks are the webhooks your organization has configured in Lumos.
`GET /v1/inline-webhooks` lists all of them, whatever their type.

A webhook's `type` says where Lumos uses it.

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description:
An integration is a service Lumos knows how to connect to, identified by an `app_class_id` such as
`okta.com` or `workspace.google.com`. This is the catalog you connect *from*. Apps you have
already connected are read through the Apps endpoints.

Only connectable integrations appear here. Software discovered in your environment that has no
Lumos integration behind it is excluded.

### Discovering how to connect

1. `GET /v1/integrations?query=google` to find the integration. The filter matches both the
   `app_class_id` and the display name, so `google` returns `workspace.google.com` and
   `cloud.google.com`.
2. `GET /v1/integrations/{app_class_id}/connection-schema` for the JSON schema of the `auth` and
   `settings` fields it expects.
3. `POST /v1/apps` with those values.

Step 2 is the point of this group: it lets you build a connect form without hardcoding one
credential shape per integration.

`GET /v1/integrations/{app_class_id}` and the connection schema return 404 for any integration the
list leaves out. The connection schema also returns 404 for an integration whose schema Lumos
cannot describe yet.

tags.name: Knowledge
tags.description:
Knowledge entries are the documents and notes Lumos agents draw on when they answer access
questions. Each entry carries a title, body, tags, and product scopes, plus an optional file
attachment.

Because of that attachment, create and update send `multipart/form-data` rather than JSON. On
update, tag and scope lists replace what was there instead of appending, and `clear_attachment=true`
removes an existing file without uploading a replacement.

`DELETE` deletes a knowledge entry. It no longer appears in list results, and you can't restore
it through the API.

Pages here are small: `page_size` defaults to 10 and is clamped to 25.

tags.name: Lifecycle Management
tags.description:
Lifecycle management covers user offboardings. An offboarding runs your organization's
offboarding workflow for one user, either right away or at a scheduled time.

- `POST /v1/lifecycle-management/user-offboardings` starts an offboarding now, or at
  `scheduled_at` when you send a future time.
- `GET /v1/lifecycle-management/user-offboardings/{user_offboarding_id}` reads one.
- `POST /v1/lifecycle-management/user-offboardings/{user_offboarding_id}:cancel` cancels one that
  is scheduled or in progress.

There is no list endpoint, so keep the `id` that create returns.

`workflow_config_id` names an offboarding workflow configuration, not a workflow from
`/v1/workflows`. Omit it to use the configuration your organization has selected for automatic
offboarding. Only organizations with the multiple offboarding workflows feature can send it. For
any other organization, a request that includes it returns 400.

Lumos enables these endpoints per organization, separately from the rest of v1, so contact your
Lumos representative to turn them on.

tags.name: Meta
tags.description:
`GET /v1/info` returns the API's current git revision, and `GET /v1/art` returns Lumos ASCII art.
Use either to check your setup.

Both require an API token. A 200 means your token works and v1 is enabled for your organization.
Lumos enables v1 per organization, so contact your Lumos representative to turn it on.

tags.name: Operations
tags.description:
An operation tracks work that continues after the request that started it has returned. These
endpoints start such work and respond with 202 and an operation:

- `POST /v1/apps/{app_uuid}:sync`
- `POST /v1/accounts:upload`
- `POST /v1/access-reviews/{review_uuid}/apps/{app_review_uuid}:sync`

Poll `GET /v1/operations/{operation_id}` until `done` is true. While `done` is false, neither
`result` nor `error` is set. Once `done` is true, exactly one of them is.

An app-sync operation shows the app's most recent sync, which can be a later run than the one you
started.

tags.name: Pre-Approval Rules
tags.description:
A pre-approval rule pre-approves matching access requests for an app.

- `GET /v1/apps/{app_uuid}/pre-approval-rules` lists an app's rules, and `POST` on the same path
  creates one.
- `GET`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` on `/v1/apps/{app_uuid}/pre-approval-rules/{pre_approval_rule_id}`
  read, update, and delete one.

If the app has been merged into another app, these endpoints work on the rules of the app it was
merged into.

Lumos enables condition-based pre-approval rules per organization, separately from the rest of v1,
so contact your Lumos representative to turn them on.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description:
A task is work Lumos assigns to a person or group, such as approving an access request or
provisioning access by hand. A workflow that creates a task waits for someone to act on it before
it continues.

### Finding tasks

`GET /v1/tasks` lists the tasks visible to you. `show_all_tasks=true` lists every task in your
organization instead. It needs permission to view every task, which the built-in Admin, Read Only
Admin, and AppStore Read Only Admin roles have, and which a custom role can also grant. Anyone
else gets a 403.

Filter with `type`, `category`, `status`, and `product_area`, whose values are lowercase and
kebab-case. For example,
`GET /v1/tasks?category=approval&product_area=appstore&status=pending` lists pending AppStore
approvals.

A task names the entitlement it grants or removes in `entitlement_id`, an Entitlement UUID.

### Acting on a task

- `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}:complete` approves an approval task, or completes another task with
  its one completion action.
- `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}:dismiss` denies an approval task, or dismisses another task without
  doing its work.
- `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}:perform-action` takes a specific action.
  `GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}/actions` lists the actions you can take and the statuses each one can
  move the task to, which are the values `transition_to` accepts.
- `POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}:reassign` changes who the task is assigned to.

tags.name: Users
tags.description:
Users are the people in your organization. These endpoints read them, and the only thing they
change is a user's Lumos roles.

- `GET /v1/users` lists users. `search` matches names and emails, and `exact_match=true`
  requires an exact match.
- `GET /v1/users/current` returns the user who owns your API token.
- `GET /v1/users/{user_id}` reads one user, and `GET /v1/users/{user_id}/accounts` lists the
  accounts that user holds.
- `GET /v1/users/{user_id}/roles` lists a user's Lumos roles.
  `POST /v1/users/{user_id}/roles/{role_name}` assigns one, and
  `DELETE /v1/users/{user_id}/roles/{role_name}` removes one. Assigning a role the user already
  has, or removing one they don't have, changes nothing.

A user who has been deleted returns the same 404 as one who doesn't exist in your organization.

tags.name: Workflows
tags.description:
A workflow is a reusable definition of the steps Lumos runs to approve a request, provision access,
or deprovision it. Create the definition here, then bind it to an app or an entitlement through
their own workflow endpoints.

### Building one

1. `GET /v1/workflow-steps?app_id={app_uuid}&type={workflow type}` to discover the steps available
   for that app in the type of workflow you will create, each with the input schema it accepts.
   Without `type`, it lists only the steps every workflow type accepts.
2. `POST /v1/workflows` with the steps you want.
3. Bind it, for example with `PUT /v1/apps/{app_uuid}/default-provisioning-workflow`.

`type` and `app_id` are fixed at creation. `PUT /v1/workflows/{workflow_id}` returns 400 for a
change to either.

### Workflows this API cannot describe

Some workflows Lumos builds for you, including the out-of-the-box provisioning defaults, contain
steps with no public representation. `GET /v1/workflows` skips them, so a page can hold fewer items
than `page_size` while more results remain. Treat an absent `next_page_token`, not a short page, as
the end of the list. Binding one of these to an app or entitlement returns 400.
